title: Crumb and Bumble's Lost Pie Tin
markdown:
The apple orchard buzzed. Leaves rustled a lovely tune. It was the day of the Great Orchard Baking Contest, and Crumb the chipmunk’s heart did a happy hop as he scampered into his burrow of dried grasses, sunshine, and acorns. “Bumble! Is the special pie tin ready? The one that makes the crusts extra-crispy?”

From a tall cherry tree, Bumble the bee-eater swooped, a flash of blue and green. “Ready and shiny, Crumb! I polished it until it winked like a little disco ball.” He landed with a soft thump.

They zipped to their baking spot under the biggest apple tree, smooth stones for seats, a hollow for bowls. Oh dear. The pie tin was not on its mossy shelf, not under leaves, not behind berry bushes. Crumb’s whiskers drooped. “Where could it be?” The judges—a wise owl and a kind old mole—would arrive any moment.

“We’ll find it,” chirped Bumble. “Let’s look together, one by one.”

First they trotted to Enfys the badger, busy digging an extra-deep den, nose already dark with soil. “A pie tin?” Enfys rumbled, not looking up. “Haven’t seen one, my dears. Just digging to keep out of the wind.”

Next they hopped to Penelope the rabbit, munching sweet clover by the fence. Her ears twitched. “Pie tin? Oh, goodness no. Just lovely leafy greens for me.”

Bumble’s sharp eyes scanned dewy grass. Crumb scurried under toadstools and behind logs. The sun climbed. Crumb’s tummy rumbled with worry. They really wanted their Honey-Apple Delight.

Bumble chirped, excited. “Look, Crumb. In the old oak. A shimmer.” High in a snug nest of moss and thistle-down sat something shiny and round: their pie tin, filled to the brim with bright yellow dandelions, a comfy bed for three tiny chirping babies.

Crumb’s heart sank. The babies looked so peaceful. The contest still needed a tin. Bumble landed gently. “Excuse me,” he chirped to the mother bird, who was returning with a plump worm. “That’s a truly beautiful nest. We’re glad you’re cozy. But that shiny tin is special to us. We need it for a very important pie, and the judges are coming soon.”

The mother bird tilted her head. She looked at her sleepy babies, then at the tin, then at Bumble and Crumb. She understood. With a soft coo she nudged the dandelions aside. “Thank you for asking so nicely.” She helped them lift the tin without disturbing her little ones, and even brushed off a few stray seeds.

Because they had asked, they had the tin. Because they had the tin, they mixed and stirred and baked with all their might. Just as the owl hooted to start judging, they pulled out a perfectly golden-brown pie, sweet smell filling the orchard.

They did not win the grand prize. They had something warmer: a tin returned by kindness, and a nest left peaceful. And so, a gentle question brings back what a snatch would spoil; friendship, like a warm pie, is the sweetest crust of all.
author: StoryGen Community
